Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of India. It will be Matthew Kuhnemann, the nightwatchman to open the innings alongside Travis Head with very less time left in the day, still a bit of a surprise. Ravichandran Ashwin has been tossed the new ball and is ready to go. Let's play...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Australia will be pretty disappointed as they were in a good positon in this Test after their batting performance. However, their bowlers were also made to work hard by the hosts and in the end they looked tired as well. Nathan Lyon bowled a marathon spell picking up three wickets while Todd Murphy also got three scalps. Matthew Kuhnemann and Mitchell Starc contributed with one each. They now trail by 91 runs and will have to bat really well as the pitch is becoming a bit spin-friendly. They need to avoid any collapses if they want to get a draw out of this as winning this match will require something extraordinary. Stay tuned as Australia's second innings is up next.

India finish on a massive total of 571 for 9! If you are thinking why the hosts are heading back after losing just nine wickets, it is because Shreyas Iyer is injured and he could not come out to bat and according to the rules there won't be any concussion substitute for him. This innings well and truly belonged to Virat Kohli who notched up his 28th Test hundred, but it was the young, Shubman Gill who set up the platform with his century early on. India were able to build six half-century or more stands which is the difference as they lead by 91 runs now.

OUT! CAUGHT! Virat Kohli holes out in the end and walks back a tad disappointed. Todd Murphy flights it up nicely outside off and Kohli goes for the slog-sweep. Kohli has to reach for it and ends up getting a top edge high in the air toward deep mid-wicket. There are two men in the deep and Marnus Labuschagne who is in front of square settles under it to take a fine catch. Kohli gets out for 186 and India finish with 571/9, leading by 91 runs.
Commentary.Howout: c Marnus Labuschagne b Todd Murphy

However, Peter Handscomb runs in, picks it up and hits bullseye at the bowler's end with Umesh Yadav nowhere near the crease. The replay confirms the same and India lose their eighth wicket.

Is that a run-out? Australia look really confident and it was a bullet of a direct hit from Peter Handscomb at the bowler's end. The replays roll in and we can clearly see that Umesh Yadav is well short of his crease while coming back for the second run and goes without facing a ball. OUT comes up on the big screen.

India seven down now!

Srikar Bharat came out after the Lunch break with aggressive intent and was heavily responsible for Cameron Green conceding 21 runs in an over which is the most in this series. Virat Kohli continued to rotate the strike without any urgency but gathered momentum once he reached his landmark. Srikar Bharat fell 6 short of his maiden half-century but Axar Patel came out to the middle and continued his remarkable form in the series. India became the first team to score 50 runs in all their six partnerships so far against Australia. Will the visitors be able to maintain their discipline and prevent the hosts from scoring freely in the final session of Day 4? Or will India put themselves in a solid position to look for a win on the final Day? Join us at 2.30 pm IST (9 am GMT) to find out.

Another session that has belonged to the Indian batters as they scored 110 runs and lost just one wicket while showing ample intent to push for a win in the last four sessions of this game. They now trail by just 8 runs and are now in complete control of this game with 5 wickets in hand. It is highly unlikely that they will lose from this position and a chunk of the credit has been given to Virat Kohli who notched up a Test century after a prolonged wait with the last one coming at the end of 2019 going into the break unbeaten on 135. The Australian bowlers look tired out in the middle and Nathan Lyon was rewarded with yet another wicket for his longest bowling spell in India and became the highest overseas wicket-taker against the hosts.

We are back for the afternoon session on the penultimate day of this Test match as the umpires make their way to the middle. The Australian players take their respective fielding positions as Virat Kohli and Srikar Bharat walk out to continue their partnership. Cameron Green has been handed the ball and will begin proceedings after Lunch. Let's go...

India got off to a steady start with Virat Kohli being rock solid at the crease. However, Ravindra Jadeja looked like he was losing patience and ultimately got out by playing a nothing shot. After that, Srikar Bharat joined Kohli, as Shreyas Iyer had gone for scans for a lower back issue, and it does not look like he would come out to bat anytime soon. Bharat supported Kohli well as they built up a partnership of 53 runs, and they will look to continue that in the post-Lunch session. Australia, on the other hand, was able to restrict the hosts from scoring freely and got their reward when Todd Murphy got rid of Jadeja early in the session. However, when Matthew Kuhnemann came into the attack, he was able to get some turn and, with his tight lines, kept the batters quiet. The Aussies will hope to make early inroads in the second session to put pressure on the hosts. Join us at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT) to see how things pan out in the second session.

Mitchell Starc is up for a quick chat. He says that he will take overcast conditions for now which could help him with some reverse swing. Adds that they have other plans too, but both the innings till now has been slow and a grind for the bowlers. Tells that the wicket does not have that much bounce, but there is some turn and he hopes that their spinners can get some early breakthroughs.

PITCH REPORT - Murali Kartik is pitchside says that the wicket is still good for batting, but the spinners got some help on Day 3 and more of the same will be on Day 4 as well. Matthew Hayden joins him and tells that the cracks have not opened up yet and they expect another Day dominated with the bat.

Cheteshwar Pujara is up for a flash interview. He says that it is good to see a wicket like this after a long time and the batters need to play on these kinds of pitches. Adds that it was nice to spend some time in the middle and get some runs, but was disappointed when he got out as there was an opportunity for a big score. Credits Shubman Gill for his century and says that he is an attacking player and he likes to play his shots. Tells that the first session will be crucial for India and if they do not lose many wickets they can try to dictate terms later on.

The visitors are slightly ahead in this game as they still have a lead of 191 runs and a flurry of wickets in the first session will get them right on top of this game. They dominated the first two Days with the bat and got a taste of their own medicine on the third Day. Their three spinners have claimed one wicket each and the onus will lie on them to get the Aussies closer to leveling the series. Will they be able to rock India’s boat with an early breakthrough? Or will the hosts continue to dominate with the bat? We will find out soon.

The Indian openers got off to a good start and found themselves clawing back into this game courtesy of a century from Shubman Gill. They still have loads of work to do if they are to overturn the deficit before finding maximum purchase from a Day 5 pitch. However, with Virat Kohli looking good at the wicket and loads of batting yet to come, it does not seem like an impossible proposition. After spending close to two Days on the field, they have done a good job to allow their bowlers some rest and a wicketless morning session will be really crucial for them to set up this game.

Hello, and a warm welcome ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of Day 4 of the fourth and final Test in the Border Gavaskar Trophy which is the furthest we have reached in any game in this series. It was the bat that reigned supreme on Day 3 as the hosts piled on 253 runs losing just 3 wickets and it was the turn of the Aussie bowlers to toil away for wickets on a surface that has been the best for batting so far. The end of this Day will provide better clarity as to which way this Test match is headed as both teams still away an opportunity to push for a win.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, three Days have passed in the fourth and final Test match of the series and it is Australia who lead by 191 runs. Given that we haven't even had two complete innings of batting done, an early shout for a draw wouldn't be a bad call but knowing the competitive nature of both sides, we might see something different on Day 4 which could change the course of the game. But will we see something out of the blue or will the cat and mouse battle continue? We shall find out. Day 4 will begin on 12th March, Sunday at 9.30 am IST (4 am GMT) but our build-up will begin a lot sooner. Cheers!

Australia won't be pleased with how the Day ended but will also know that there is still hardly anything in it for the bowlers. They managed to pick up a wicket in the final session thanks to Nathan Lyon who put in a real shift under the warm sun. Matthew Kuhnemann and Todd Murphy did well to keep the runs in check but failed to create much opportunities. Mitchell Starc couldn't quite get the ball to swing or reverse and wasn't effective either. They will hope that a few more cracks open up on Day 4 and the spinners can have a fruitful morning session.

India came into the final session having lost a wicket just before the Tea break. Shubman Gill was already well-set but Virat Kohli was new at the crease and Gill did well to score runs a bit freely, allowing Kohli to settle down at the other end. Once Kohli too started to score, India looked in a good position but Gill had a few fitness issues and eventually got out. After that the scoring rate slowed down but Kohli was able to bring up his first half-century of the tour and Ravindra Jadeja supported him well at the other end. They made sure India didn't lose further wickets and went into Day 4 in a good position.

Session Summary - 36 overs, 101 runs and 1 wicket! Day 3 is generally known as the moving day but if we look at this game, it is left very much in the balance with neither side able to force the issue. With a track suited for the batters and is a slower one as well, it is a test of everyone's patience and at the moment both teams have remained resolute. Something will have to give early on Day 4 for either side to press the issue for a favorable result.

We are back for the final session on Day 3! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of Australia. Nathan Lyon hasn't come out with the team and it is Matt Renshaw who has come on as a substitute. Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli are set to resume their stay on the crease. It will be Todd Murphy to continue with the ball after the break. Let's play...
... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ...

A good end to the session for Australia! However, India have managed to see through this one, losing only one wicket and scoring 59 runs. Shubman Gill completed his century as well, which is his first against the Aussies, and Cheteshwar Pujara supported him well from the other end. Their partnership was worth 113 runs, and that has put the hosts in a stable position. Australia, on the other hand, tried a lot of things, changing their fields and ends of bowlers, but nothing really worked for them until the second last over of the session, when Todd Murphy got rid of Cheteshwar Pujara. The captaincy from Steven Smith has been very proactive which helped them to lower the scoring rate of the hosts, and ultimately got their reward. The last over of the session saw Nathan Lyon trouble Virat Kohli a bit, and they will look to make early inroads when they come out in the last session while India will hope for another big partership. Join us at 2.30 pm IST (9 am GMT) to see how things pan out.

Pitch Report - Murali Karthik is joined by Mitchell Johnson who says that the pitch will be very similar to Day 1 and 2. Ravichandran Ashwin is up for a chat and he says that they have put two days of handwork on a pitch that had very little so to get the wickets was rewarding. Claims that even Travis Head’s wicket seemed like a rash shot but he saw a lot of videos and says that helped make plans for his dismissal. Mentions that it is not about bowling wicket-taking deliveries but about making the batter uncomfortable and that will yield wickets. India were made to toil and toil hard on Day 2 but Ravichandran Ashwin showed his class and picked up six wickets ensuring the Australian total was kept under 500 runs but India would have liked for the others to contribute more as at one point they had the chance to keep the opposition to around 400 runs. They will now look to start fresh on Day 3 and break the opening stand at the earliest.
